evidence: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:485-492 calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without await. Before this PR, the DB deletes were collected and awaited through prismaPromises. Now the DB write (update cancelled=true or delete) runs inside the un-awaited helper, so the API can respond, and a serverless function can be frozen, before the write finishes. If the write never lands, the cron will not cancel the email. The claim that errors are 'silently lost' is overstated: both helpers catch and console.log their errors (emailReminderManager.ts:197-235, smsReminderManager.ts:177-190). Fix: collect the promises and await Promise.all.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964-975: the try/catch wraps a synchronous forEach over async calls, so it can never catch their rejections. In practice the helpers never reject because they catch internally (emailReminderManager.ts, smsReminderManager.ts), so no error escapes either way. The try/catch is dead code, and the real concern is the missing await. Suggested fix: await Promise.all(reminders.map(...)) and drop or keep the try/catch.

handleNewBooking.ts:968 calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true). In emailReminderManager.ts, when immediateDelete is set the helper only POSTs /v3/user/scheduled_sends with status 'cancel' and returns, so the workflowReminder row is never deleted or flagged. The original booking is not deleted on reschedule, so the row is not cascade-removed (schema.prisma WorkflowReminder.booking onDelete: Cascade) and stays orphaned with scheduled=true. Worse, reschedules are frequent, and this path uses the direct SendGrid cancel that the PR description says fails after 100 pending cancellations, so the bug stays open for reschedules. bookings.tsx requestReschedule uses the deferred path (no immediateDelete), which is inconsistent with this call.

scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-50 filters only on cancelled:true and scheduledDate. cancelled=true is only ever set in deleteScheduledEmailReminder (emailReminderManager.ts), and every call site invokes that only for WorkflowMethods.EMAIL. deleteScheduledSMSReminder deletes the row instead (smsReminderManager.ts:177-190). No SMS row can have cancelled=true, so the scenario can't happen today. Adding method: EMAIL would be cheap defensive hardening.

The type is nullable (schema.prisma: referenceId String?), but emailReminderManager.ts deleteScheduledEmailReminder deletes the row and returns early when !referenceId, before it would set cancelled=true. So every row the cron picks up with cancelled:true has a referenceId, and the scenario can't occur. Adding a `referenceId: { not: null }` filter or a guard would only be type-level hardening.

scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53-77: a single try wraps the whole for-loop, so one SendGrid failure skips every remaining reminder. The second half of the claim is wrong: prisma.workflowReminder.delete returns a lazy PrismaPromise that only runs when awaited or then'd. On a throw, Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete) is never reached, so NO deletions run, including those for batches that were already cancelled. That is arguably worse: those rows keep cancelled=true, get retried every 15 min, and the repeat cancel POST on a batch that already has a status can fail again. The whole queue can then stall behind one bad reminder. Fix: put a try/catch around each reminder and delete the row right after its cancel succeeds.

WorkflowStepContainer.tsx 'send_code' Button: disabled={numberVerified || false}, with no sendVerificationCodeMutation.isLoading check, while the Verify button does use verifyPhoneNumberMutation.isLoading. The claim is accurate, but the block was only re-indented in this PR (the isSenderIdNeeded wrapper was removed). The behavior is pre-existing and outside the PR's scope.

WorkflowStepContainer.tsx: placeholder="Verification code" and the literal 'Verify' button label are hardcoded, while neighbouring labels use t() (t("send_code"), t("phone_number"), t("number_verified")). This is pre-existing code that the PR only moved, so it's a low-priority follow-up.

emailReminderManager.ts immediateDelete branch: POST cancel, then return, with no prisma delete. It is true that the row is not deleted. 'Critical' is overstated. Two of the three immediateDelete call sites, workflows.tsx:212 (delete workflow, followed by workflow.deleteMany) and workflows.tsx:521 (deleted step, followed by workflowStep.delete), are cleaned up by the onDelete: Cascade on WorkflowReminder.workflowStep. Only handleNewBooking.ts:968 leaves orphans. Those rows are harmless to the cron, which only selects scheduled:false or cancelled:true, but they accumulate. Fix: delete the row after the cancel succeeds in the immediate branch.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488-494: the helpers are called in forEach without await, and the previous `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` was removed. The cancelled=true flag write is therefore fire-and-forget. If it's lost, the old booking's email still goes out, which is a stale reminder for a rescheduled booking. 'Duplicate notifications' is a stretch because the new booking gets its own reminders only when the attendee rebooks. Fix: await Promise.all over the mapped promises.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:1-10 changed `import type { Prisma, PrismaPromise }` into a value import. PrismaPromise is only used as a type (line 342), and Prisma is not used at runtime in the file. packages/config/eslint-preset.js:35 enables @typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports, so this breaks the repo lint rule and reverts a deliberate type-only import. Restore `import type`. Prettier formatting also regressed (missing trailing comma after Prisma).

workflows.tsx:212-218 (delete), 376-382 (activeOn change) and 572-579 (edited steps) invoke the helpers in forEach without await. Before this PR the DB deletes were awaited (Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise), await deleteMany), and those awaits were removed. In the delete paths, workflow.deleteMany/workflowStep.delete run concurrently, so SMS prisma.delete can hit P2025. That error is caught and logged, not silent. Un-awaited SendGrid/Twilio cancels can also be cut off in serverless. The 'silently' wording is overstated, but the missing await is real.

workflows.tsx:212 and 521 do pass immediateDelete=true, which uses the direct SendGrid cancel that is capped at 100 pending cancellations. Here that choice is necessary: the workflow/step is deleted right afterwards, and WorkflowReminder cascades on workflowStep (schema.prisma), so a deferred cancelled=true flag would be deleted before the cron could act on it. The concern about the 100-cap is legitimate. A correct fix would need a different design, such as detaching reminders from the step or cancelling via the cron before deleting, not just removing the flag.

WorkflowStepContainer.tsx: the send-code and Verify onClick handlers call mutate with `form.getValues(...sendTo) || ""` and verificationCode without client-side checks. The `required` attribute does nothing without a form submit. This is pre-existing code that the PR only moved, and the server mutations validate the input. The only cost is a wasted round-trip, so this is a UX nicety.

schema.prisma WorkflowReminder has no @@index (only the id PK and the referenceId unique). The new cron query (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-50) filters on cancelled + scheduledDate, but so do the existing queries on method/scheduled/scheduledDate, which are also unindexed. The query runs every 15 min, and rows are deleted after sending or cancelling, so the table stays small. A (cancelled, scheduledDate) index is a speculative optimization, not a defect introduced here.
